title: Founder case: Zappos tests before buying stock

sources.claim: Zappos founder Nick Swinmurn tested online shoe sales by photographing shoes in local stores and, when an order came in, buying the pair from the store and shipping it, before holding inventory.

sections.skill: Apply a documented test: sell before holding inventory

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how did Swinmurn fill early orders?

choices.text: He had a factory make each pair to order.
He shipped shoes from a large warehouse he owned.
He asked customers to pick up shoes at his home.
He bought the shoes from local stores and shipped them.

questions.correct_answer: He bought the shoes from local stores and shipped them.
questions.intro: Documented history: Zappos founder Nick Swinmurn tested whether people would buy shoes online before holding any inventory. He photographed shoes at local stores and posted them online; when someone ordered a pair, he bought it from the store at full price and shipped it. Lesson drawn by this course (an interpretation): you can test demand before investing in stock, even if each early sale earns little or loses money, because the goal of the test is to learn. One success story does not guarantee the same result for another business.
questions.feedback: He bought each ordered pair at full price from the store.

questions.intro: Imagine opening a small bakery stand. One way: bake 200 loaves and hope they sell. Another way: take orders first, then bake only what was ordered.
